title: When a Feed Invoice Falls Due and What an Overdue Feed Account Carries
content:
A feed invoice falls due the programme's terms in calendar days after the invoice date, a payment landing on the due date itself still being on time; a cash programme carries no terms and the load is paid for as it leaves. An invoice still unpaid after the programme's grace period, counted in whole calendar days from the due date, carries the programme's late charge once and then the programme's monthly service charge for as long as it stands unpaid.

## The clock the charge is read off

Within the Feed and Animal Nutrition Programmes the clock runs from the invoice date carried on the mill's own record of the invoice, from which the due date is the programme's terms in calendar days. The grace period is then counted in whole calendar days from that due date, and the duration counted is the grace the programme's terms of account set. The charge attaches only once the grace has run out: a day that is not later than the last day of the grace is inside it, and the late charge is raised on the day after the grace ends. What is looked at is the invoice by its own number, the invoice date it carries and the money standing on it, all as the mill's records show them rather than as the member recounts them.

*Hypothetical.* An invoice dated the first of a month on a programme whose terms are fifteen calendar days falls due on the sixteenth. Where the programme's grace is ten calendar days, an invoice paid on the twenty-sixth is paid inside the grace and carries no late charge; unpaid into the twenty-seventh, it carries the late charge once, and the monthly service charge runs on it for as long as it stands unpaid.

## How money is applied, and what arrears stop

Payments may reach the mill only by the methods the programme allows and are applied oldest invoice first unless the member names an invoice. Feed is not delivered on a programme whose combined balance has passed its limit, and the mill does not extend credit at the loading dock. Where a member's grain settlement is due to clear the balance within days, whether to run the load anyway is a judgement for the credit department and not one this rule settles.

## Points of judgement

| The position | How it reads |
| --- | --- |
| Payment lands on the due date itself | On time |
| Payment lands inside the grace, after the due date | No late charge |
| The invoice stands unpaid once the grace has run | The late charge once, then the monthly service charge while it stands unpaid |
| The programme carries no terms | The load is paid for as it leaves |
